analysis.title: GS Healthcare Trading Preview 11.3.26
key_insights: Choppy first session of November: outsized EPS moves in consumer-levered healthcare names (IDXX +22%), a calendar effect on negative-momentum names (Medtech outperformed), and a TMT/AI tape that sold off through the day and pulled Tools/CROs lower in sympathy.
Tools names reported higher premarket on 11/3: RVTY +9% and WAT +6% per the desk's focus paragraph. The RVTY item in the same note says the stock was bid up 11% on very light volume.
The desk expects Midterms/election themes to stay in focus, with healthcare services the area of focus.
GS PB October hedge fund data: TMT L/S funds lost 12.6% in October (up 5.1% YTD), while Health Care L/S funds lost 1.4% (up 8.5% YTD).
US Health Care stocks were net bought for the first time in 3 months, driven by risk-off activity, with short covers outpacing long sales 1.5 to 1.
Biotech, Health Care Providers & Services and Pharmaceuticals were the most net bought subsectors in dollar terms. Health Care Equipment and Life Sciences Tools & Services were the most net sold.
US Health Care long/short ratio is 2.40, in the 6th percentile vs the past year and the 26th percentile vs the past five years.
Defensive sectors were net bought for the first time in 7 months, with Staples and Health Care both net bought and little net activity in Utilities.
PFE reported a 3Q beat and raised 2026 guidance, and named Cecile Guegan permanent CFO after she served as interim CFO since mid August.
WAT beat on organic growth and raised FY organic revenue growth guidance. It will give a 2027 growth framework on the conference call, covering reshoring, synergies and AI-related demand drivers.
RVTY beat on revenue and the Life Sciences segment, and raised FY26 revenue and adjusted EPS guidance.
VRTX reported a 3Q in line with GSe and consensus on revenue. Alyftrek beat, Journavx missed, Casgevy beat, and IgAN approval is the focus into 4Q and beyond.

BMRN missed slightly on revenue, with a Voxzogo miss caused by ex-US order timing shifting to 4Q. Pombiliti + Opfolda was strong as management made extra inventory available amid SNY supply constraints in Europe.
TEVA beat on 3Q revenue and EPS, driven by Treanda and Bendeka, and raised its FY revenue forecast.
AMRX beat on 3Q adjusted EBITDA and net revenue, with strength in both generics and specialty segments and stronger margins.

JAZZ beat on 3Q revenue and raised and narrowed FY26 guidance for Sleep and total revenue. Ziihera in 1L GEA drove a 3x MoM increase in new ordering accounts and a 40% MoM increase in average vial demand per selling day after one month on the market.
The XLV vs SMH pair shows healthcare outperforming semiconductors, back to early April levels.

sector_views.rationale: The desk reports Health Care L/S funds lost 1.4% in October and US Health Care stocks were net bought for the first time in 3 months, with the L/S ratio at the 6th percentile vs the past year.
TMT L/S funds lost 12.6% in October, and the AI/TMT tape sold off through the day on 11/2, pulling Tools/CROs lower in sympathy.

earnings_insights: WAT 3Q reported 11/3: revenue $1.77B vs $1.75B consensus, organic constant-currency growth +10% vs 9% consensus, EPS $4.10 vs $4.00 consensus. FY organic revenue growth guidance raised to 9.1%-9.7% from 7%-9%.

RVTY 3Q26 reported: revenue $729mn ($710mn pro forma) vs FactSet consensus $695mn and GSe $729mn ($697mn pro forma). Pro forma organic growth was 7%. FY26 revenue guidance raised to $2.86bn (~5% organic) from $2.83bn-$2.86bn. Adjusted operating margin guidance 28.8% vs 28.7% prior. Adjusted EPS guidance $5.40-$5.45 from $5.30-$5.40.

PFE 3Q reported: revenue $16.6B vs $15.9B consensus, EPS $0.87 vs $0.74 prior estimate. 2026 revenue guidance raised to $62B-$64B from $60.5B-$62.5B, EPS guidance raised to $2.95-$3.05 from $2.80-$3.00. Beat was broad at product level excluding Prevnar and Comirnaty.

VRTX 3Q reported: revenue $3.4bn in line with GSe and company-compiled consensus. Cystic fibrosis revenue $3,273mn vs GSe/consensus $3,292mn/$3,274mn. Alyftrek $706mn vs GSe/consensus $635mn/$651mn. Journavx $58mn vs GSe/consensus $70mn/$65mn, hurt by a one-time $7-8mn impact from securing Medicare Part D access. Casgevy $99mn vs GSe/consensus $85mn/$77mn. Non-GAAP EPS $4.76, reflecting higher expenses tied to the CRNX acquisition.

BMRN 3Q reported: revenue $1,025mn vs GSe/FactSet consensus $1,031mn/$1,022mn. Metabolic conditions revenue $744mn vs GSe/consensus $749mn/$736mn. Voxzogo $245mn vs GSe/consensus $257mn/$258mn on ex-US order timing shifting to 4Q. Non-GAAP EPS $0.23 vs GSe/consensus $0.19/($0.09), affected by IPR&D from the Alesta Therapeutics acquisition.

TEVA Q3 reported: EPS 86c vs 72c estimate, revenue $4.4B vs $4.24B estimate. FY revenue forecast tweaked to $16.7B-$17.0B from $16.5B-$16.85B. AUSTEDO global revenues were $751 million and AJOVY global revenues were $269 million. The source text lists two raised 2026 outlooks, $2.55B-$2.65B from $2.45B-$2.60B and $930M-$960M from $850M-$870M, but the product each applies to is garbled in the source text.
AMRX 3Q reported: adjusted EBITDA $207mn vs GSe/Visible Alpha consensus $186mn/$187mn. Net revenue $863mn vs GSe/consensus $814mn/$811mn, about 10% YoY growth.

JAZZ 3Q reported: revenue $1.24bn vs GSe/FactSet consensus $1.17bn/$1.21bn. FY26 Sleep guidance raised and narrowed to $2.125-2.175bn (+7% YoY at midpoint, new GSe $2.147bn). Total revenue guidance $4.775-4.850bn (+13% YoY at midpoint, new GSe $4.790bn).

IDXX moved +22% on 11/2 on EPS, the desk's example of outsized EPS moves in consumer-levered corners of the sector. The desk lists a GS research note on IDXX stating innovation and execution offset broader market softness.

KRYS 3Q EPS: GS research title says pipeline delays overshadowed a solid quarter. ABBV: GS research title says steady results delivered with an eye toward 2027 growth. MRNA: GS 3Q earnings preview notes the Phase 3 melanoma win, with focus shifting to RCC and the platform.

Desk implied earnings moves are largest for QDEL (20.8%), TNDM (18.1%), INSP (14.0%), GH (14.4%), TXG (13.8%), ADPT (11.5%), PODD (11.0%), and RVTY (10.6%). The positioning table's source line is dated 7/20/2026, so the scores may be stale.
